chapter: New Orleans arrival, jazz and Fazola
title: Hearing and learning New Orleans jazz, pick-up bands, Fazola
summary: Lured to New Orleans by its jazz reputation, he learns the two-beat, plays Dixieland on weekend pick-up jobs, meets Fazola and plays Broadway shows at the Civic.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. Just about that time. About forty-eight. I'd have to look it up in the files because, boy, I'm very bad with dates. Mm-hmm. I don't mean dates with girls, but I mean, as far as nineteen this, nineteen that, and June, and January. Yeah. Did you hear any jazz when you came down here? Oh, yeah. I certainly did. Uh, in fact, uh, that's one of the reasons why I was lured down here, because I had heard of the famous New Orleans jazz. Mm-hmm. And, of course, being a musician, you'd, you'd always want to hear something different, something new. And I was very impressed by it, and I also got to play it, you know, and it was quite difficult for me for a while to do it, but then I, I began to feel that two beat, you know. Yeah. And, uh, before you knew it, I, I was playing every Saturday nights, Friday nights, Sunday nights, and before you know it, I was playing Dixieland. Who were you playing with? Oh, I was playing with a lot of pick-up-the-last-minute bands, you know, out of the Union. And, uh, most of them, that's what they were. And, of course, there was, there was always interesting musicians in it. And so happened that, uh, I was playing Jobs, and there was, they were in Fazola playing clarinet, you know. And, uh, all things like that kind of scared me, because I knew he was a famous guy, and here I was, practically a greenhorn. At least I considered myself that. And I also got to play, uh, all the shows that came in at the Civic. Broadway shows, musical productions, you know. So, before you knew it, there I was.
